  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### The One Thing That Can Silently Break Everything\nThe idempotency design (watch item #1) is the only open significant flag. Get this right in T3 or every retry creates duplicates. The fix: client continues sending its stable idempotency_key (already at createTask.ts:39). For batch resolvers that expand 1 request into N tasks, the server derives per-task keys as `hash(clientIdempotencyKey + taskIndex)`. This is deterministic \u2014 retries produce the same N keys. Do NOT generate fresh UUIDs server-side.\n\n### Phasing Strategy\nThe plan's 7-phase structure exists for a reason \u2014 respect it:\n- **Foundation (T1-T6)** must land and be tested before any resolver. The dispatch + batch insert + response parsing form the platform.\n- **Type relocation (T7-T9)** is independent of foundation and can be parallelized with T1-T6. Do it early \u2014 it's low-risk and prevents compilation breakage when families are deleted later.\n- **Simple resolvers (T10-T12)** validate the architecture cheaply. If upscale or videoEnhance break, fix the framework before attempting complex resolvers.\n- **Cleanup (T22-T24)** is ONLY safe after ALL callers are migrated. The raw path stays alive until every family is done.\n\n### Parallelization Opportunities\n- T7, T8, T9 are fully independent of each other and of T1-T6.\n- T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T19, T20, T21 all depend only on T5 and can be parallelized.\n- T16 depends on T5 + T7; T17 depends on T5 + T9; T18 depends on T5 + T8.\n\n### Deno Compatibility Pitfalls\nThe edge function runs in Deno, not Node. When porting:\n- No `crypto.randomUUID()` without importing from std \u2014 use Deno's `crypto.randomUUID()` directly.\n- No `process.env` \u2014 use `Deno.env.get()`.\n- No relative imports without extensions \u2014 all imports need `.ts` suffix.\n- No npm packages unless already in the edge function's import map.\n\n### Deletion Safety Protocol (T23)\nDelete in small batches, running `npx tsc --noEmit` after each:\n1. First batch: family directories (imageUpscale/, videoEnhance/, zImageTurboI2I/) \u2014 simplest, no shared exports.\n2. Second batch: imageGeneration/ directory (after confirming types fully relocated).\n3. Third batch: joinClips/, individualTravelSegment/ directories.\n4. Fourth batch: travel creation files (createTravelBetweenImagesTask.ts, payloadBuilder.ts) \u2014 highest risk due to adjacent read-side files.\n5. Fifth batch: imageEditing files, crossfade, creation-only utilities.\n\n### createInpaintingTaskWorkflow.ts Double-Edit Risk\nThis file is a caller for BOTH magicEdit (T14) and maskedEdit (T15). If these tasks are done by different executors or in parallel, coordinate edits to avoid conflicts. Recommend doing T14 and T15 sequentially, or having one executor handle both.\n\n### What to Snapshot Before Migration\nBefore starting any resolver, capture the exact DB params for each task type by creating one task of each type through the current client-side path. Save these as JSON snapshots. After each resolver migration, compare the new server-generated params against the snapshot. Workers are not being changed \u2014 param compatibility is the hard constraint."

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### The One Thing That Can Silently Break Everything\nThe idempotency design (watch item #1) is the only open significant flag. Get this right in T3 or every retry creates duplicates. The fix: client continues sending its stable idempotency_key (already at createTask.ts:39). For batch resolvers that expand 1 request into N tasks, the server derives per-task keys as `hash(clientIdempotencyKey + taskIndex)`. This is deterministic \u2014 retries produce the same N keys. Do NOT generate fresh UUIDs server-side.\n\n### Phasing Strategy\nThe plan's 7-phase structure exists for a reason \u2014 respect it:\n- **Foundation (T1-T6)** must land and be tested before any resolver. The dispatch + batch insert + response parsing form the platform.\n- **Type relocation (T7-T9)** is independent of foundation and can be parallelized with T1-T6. Do it early \u2014 it's low-risk and prevents compilation breakage when families are deleted later.\n- **Simple resolvers (T10-T12)** validate the architecture cheaply. If upscale or videoEnhance break, fix the framework before attempting complex resolvers.\n- **Cleanup (T22-T24)** is ONLY safe after ALL callers are migrated. The raw path stays alive until every family is done.\n\n### Parallelization Opportunities\n- T7, T8, T9 are fully independent of each other and of T1-T6.\n- T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T19, T20, T21 all depend only on T5 and can be parallelized.\n- T16 depends on T5 + T7; T17 depends on T5 + T9; T18 depends on T5 + T8.\n\n### Deno Compatibility Pitfalls\nThe edge function runs in Deno, not Node. When porting:\n- No `crypto.randomUUID()` without importing from std \u2014 use Deno's `crypto.randomUUID()` directly.\n- No `process.env` \u2014 use `Deno.env.get()`.\n- No relative imports without extensions \u2014 all imports need `.ts` suffix.\n- No npm packages unless already in the edge function's import map.\n\n### Deletion Safety Protocol (T23)\nDelete in small batches, running `npx tsc --noEmit` after each:\n1. First batch: family directories (imageUpscale/, videoEnhance/, zImageTurboI2I/) \u2014 simplest, no shared exports.\n2. Second batch: imageGeneration/ directory (after confirming types fully relocated).\n3. Third batch: joinClips/, individualTravelSegment/ directories.\n4. Fourth batch: travel creation files (createTravelBetweenImagesTask.ts, payloadBuilder.ts) \u2014 highest risk due to adjacent read-side files.\n5. Fifth batch: imageEditing files, crossfade, creation-only utilities.\n\n### createInpaintingTaskWorkflow.ts Double-Edit Risk\nThis file is a caller for BOTH magicEdit (T14) and maskedEdit (T15). If these tasks are done by different executors or in parallel, coordinate edits to avoid conflicts. Recommend doing T14 and T15 sequentially, or having one executor handle both.\n\n### What to Snapshot Before Migration\nBefore starting any resolver, capture the exact DB params for each task type by creating one task of each type through the current client-side path. Save these as JSON snapshots. After each resolver migration, compare the new server-generated params against the snapshot. Workers are not being changed \u2014 param compatibility is the hard constraint."

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### The One Thing That Can Silently Break Everything\nThe idempotency design (watch item #1) is the only open significant flag. Get this right in T3 or every retry creates duplicates. The fix: client continues sending its stable idempotency_key (already at createTask.ts:39). For batch resolvers that expand 1 request into N tasks, the server derives per-task keys as `hash(clientIdempotencyKey + taskIndex)`. This is deterministic \u2014 retries produce the same N keys. Do NOT generate fresh UUIDs server-side.\n\n### Phasing Strategy\nThe plan's 7-phase structure exists for a reason \u2014 respect it:\n- **Foundation (T1-T6)** must land and be tested before any resolver. The dispatch + batch insert + response parsing form the platform.\n- **Type relocation (T7-T9)** is independent of foundation and can be parallelized with T1-T6. Do it early \u2014 it's low-risk and prevents compilation breakage when families are deleted later.\n- **Simple resolvers (T10-T12)** validate the architecture cheaply. If upscale or videoEnhance break, fix the framework before attempting complex resolvers.\n- **Cleanup (T22-T24)** is ONLY safe after ALL callers are migrated. The raw path stays alive until every family is done.\n\n### Parallelization Opportunities\n- T7, T8, T9 are fully independent of each other and of T1-T6.\n- T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T19, T20, T21 all depend only on T5 and can be parallelized.\n- T16 depends on T5 + T7; T17 depends on T5 + T9; T18 depends on T5 + T8.\n\n### Deno Compatibility Pitfalls\nThe edge function runs in Deno, not Node. When porting:\n- No `crypto.randomUUID()` without importing from std \u2014 use Deno's `crypto.randomUUID()` directly.\n- No `process.env` \u2014 use `Deno.env.get()`.\n- No relative imports without extensions \u2014 all imports need `.ts` suffix.\n- No npm packages unless already in the edge function's import map.\n\n### Deletion Safety Protocol (T23)\nDelete in small batches, running `npx tsc --noEmit` after each:\n1. First batch: family directories (imageUpscale/, videoEnhance/, zImageTurboI2I/) \u2014 simplest, no shared exports.\n2. Second batch: imageGeneration/ directory (after confirming types fully relocated).\n3. Third batch: joinClips/, individualTravelSegment/ directories.\n4. Fourth batch: travel creation files (createTravelBetweenImagesTask.ts, payloadBuilder.ts) \u2014 highest risk due to adjacent read-side files.\n5. Fifth batch: imageEditing files, crossfade, creation-only utilities.\n\n### createInpaintingTaskWorkflow.ts Double-Edit Risk\nThis file is a caller for BOTH magicEdit (T14) and maskedEdit (T15). If these tasks are done by different executors or in parallel, coordinate edits to avoid conflicts. Recommend doing T14 and T15 sequentially, or having one executor handle both.\n\n### What to Snapshot Before Migration\nBefore starting any resolver, capture the exact DB params for each task type by creating one task of each type through the current client-side path. Save these as JSON snapshots. After each resolver migration, compare the new server-generated params against the snapshot. Workers are not being changed \u2014 param compatibility is the hard constraint."

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### The One Thing That Can Silently Break Everything\nThe idempotency design (watch item #1) is the only open significant flag. Get this right in T3 or every retry creates duplicates. The fix: client continues sending its stable idempotency_key (already at createTask.ts:39). For batch resolvers that expand 1 request into N tasks, the server derives per-task keys as `hash(clientIdempotencyKey + taskIndex)`. This is deterministic \u2014 retries produce the same N keys. Do NOT generate fresh UUIDs server-side.\n\n### Phasing Strategy\nThe plan's 7-phase structure exists for a reason \u2014 respect it:\n- **Foundation (T1-T6)** must land and be tested before any resolver. The dispatch + batch insert + response parsing form the platform.\n- **Type relocation (T7-T9)** is independent of foundation and can be parallelized with T1-T6. Do it early \u2014 it's low-risk and prevents compilation breakage when families are deleted later.\n- **Simple resolvers (T10-T12)** validate the architecture cheaply. If upscale or videoEnhance break, fix the framework before attempting complex resolvers.\n- **Cleanup (T22-T24)** is ONLY safe after ALL callers are migrated. The raw path stays alive until every family is done.\n\n### Parallelization Opportunities\n- T7, T8, T9 are fully independent of each other and of T1-T6.\n- T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T19, T20, T21 all depend only on T5 and can be parallelized.\n- T16 depends on T5 + T7; T17 depends on T5 + T9; T18 depends on T5 + T8.\n\n### Deno Compatibility Pitfalls\nThe edge function runs in Deno, not Node. When porting:\n- No `crypto.randomUUID()` without importing from std \u2014 use Deno's `crypto.randomUUID()` directly.\n- No `process.env` \u2014 use `Deno.env.get()`.\n- No relative imports without extensions \u2014 all imports need `.ts` suffix.\n- No npm packages unless already in the edge function's import map.\n\n### Deletion Safety Protocol (T23)\nDelete in small batches, running `npx tsc --noEmit` after each:\n1. First batch: family directories (imageUpscale/, videoEnhance/, zImageTurboI2I/) \u2014 simplest, no shared exports.\n2. Second batch: imageGeneration/ directory (after confirming types fully relocated).\n3. Third batch: joinClips/, individualTravelSegment/ directories.\n4. Fourth batch: travel creation files (createTravelBetweenImagesTask.ts, payloadBuilder.ts) \u2014 highest risk due to adjacent read-side files.\n5. Fifth batch: imageEditing files, crossfade, creation-only utilities.\n\n### createInpaintingTaskWorkflow.ts Double-Edit Risk\nThis file is a caller for BOTH magicEdit (T14) and maskedEdit (T15). If these tasks are done by different executors or in parallel, coordinate edits to avoid conflicts. Recommend doing T14 and T15 sequentially, or having one executor handle both.\n\n### What to Snapshot Before Migration\nBefore starting any resolver, capture the exact DB params for each task type by creating one task of each type through the current client-side path. Save these as JSON snapshots. After each resolver migration, compare the new server-generated params against the snapshot. Workers are not being changed \u2014 param compatibility is the hard constraint."

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### The One Thing That Can Silently Break Everything\nThe idempotency design (watch item #1) is the only open significant flag. Get this right in T3 or every retry creates duplicates. The fix: client continues sending its stable idempotency_key (already at createTask.ts:39). For batch resolvers that expand 1 request into N tasks, the server derives per-task keys as `hash(clientIdempotencyKey + taskIndex)`. This is deterministic \u2014 retries produce the same N keys. Do NOT generate fresh UUIDs server-side.\n\n### Phasing Strategy\nThe plan's 7-phase structure exists for a reason \u2014 respect it:\n- **Foundation (T1-T6)** must land and be tested before any resolver. The dispatch + batch insert + response parsing form the platform.\n- **Type relocation (T7-T9)** is independent of foundation and can be parallelized with T1-T6. Do it early \u2014 it's low-risk and prevents compilation breakage when families are deleted later.\n- **Simple resolvers (T10-T12)** validate the architecture cheaply. If upscale or videoEnhance break, fix the framework before attempting complex resolvers.\n- **Cleanup (T22-T24)** is ONLY safe after ALL callers are migrated. The raw path stays alive until every family is done.\n\n### Parallelization Opportunities\n- T7, T8, T9 are fully independent of each other and of T1-T6.\n- T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T19, T20, T21 all depend only on T5 and can be parallelized.\n- T16 depends on T5 + T7; T17 depends on T5 + T9; T18 depends on T5 + T8.\n\n### Deno Compatibility Pitfalls\nThe edge function runs in Deno, not Node. When porting:\n- No `crypto.randomUUID()` without importing from std \u2014 use Deno's `crypto.randomUUID()` directly.\n- No `process.env` \u2014 use `Deno.env.get()`.\n- No relative imports without extensions \u2014 all imports need `.ts` suffix.\n- No npm packages unless already in the edge function's import map.\n\n### Deletion Safety Protocol (T23)\nDelete in small batches, running `npx tsc --noEmit` after each:\n1. First batch: family directories (imageUpscale/, videoEnhance/, zImageTurboI2I/) \u2014 simplest, no shared exports.\n2. Second batch: imageGeneration/ directory (after confirming types fully relocated).\n3. Third batch: joinClips/, individualTravelSegment/ directories.\n4. Fourth batch: travel creation files (createTravelBetweenImagesTask.ts, payloadBuilder.ts) \u2014 highest risk due to adjacent read-side files.\n5. Fifth batch: imageEditing files, crossfade, creation-only utilities.\n\n### createInpaintingTaskWorkflow.ts Double-Edit Risk\nThis file is a caller for BOTH magicEdit (T14) and maskedEdit (T15). If these tasks are done by different executors or in parallel, coordinate edits to avoid conflicts. Recommend doing T14 and T15 sequentially, or having one executor handle both.\n\n### What to Snapshot Before Migration\nBefore starting any resolver, capture the exact DB params for each task type by creating one task of each type through the current client-side path. Save these as JSON snapshots. After each resolver migration, compare the new server-generated params against the snapshot. Workers are not being changed \u2014 param compatibility is the hard constraint."

  "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### The One Thing That Can Silently Break Everything\nThe idempotency design (watch item #1) is the only open significant flag. Get this right in T3 or every retry creates duplicates. The fix: client continues sending its stable idempotency_key (already at createTask.ts:39). For batch resolvers that expand 1 request into N tasks, the server derives per-task keys as `hash(clientIdempotencyKey + taskIndex)`. This is deterministic \u2014 retries produce the same N keys. Do NOT generate fresh UUIDs server-side.\n\n### Phasing Strategy\nThe plan's 7-phase structure exists for a reason \u2014 respect it:\n- **Foundation (T1-T6)** must land and be tested before any resolver. The dispatch + batch insert + response parsing form the platform.\n- **Type relocation (T7-T9)** is independent of foundation and can be parallelized with T1-T6. Do it early \u2014 it's low-risk and prevents compilation breakage when families are deleted later.\n- **Simple resolvers (T10-T12)** validate the architecture cheaply. If upscale or videoEnhance break, fix the framework before attempting complex resolvers.\n- **Cleanup (T22-T24)** is ONLY safe after ALL callers are migrated. The raw path stays alive until every family is done.\n\n### Parallelization Opportunities\n- T7, T8, T9 are fully independent of each other and of T1-T6.\n- T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T19, T20, T21 all depend only on T5 and can be parallelized.\n- T16 depends on T5 + T7; T17 depends on T5 + T9; T18 depends on T5 + T8.\n\n### Deno Compatibility Pitfalls\nThe edge function runs in Deno, not Node. When porting:\n- No `crypto.randomUUID()` without importing from std \u2014 use Deno's `crypto.randomUUID()` directly.\n- No `process.env` \u2014 use `Deno.env.get()`.\n- No relative imports without extensions \u2014 all imports need `.ts` suffix.\n- No npm packages unless already in the edge function's import map.\n\n### Deletion Safety Protocol (T23)\nDelete in small batches, running `npx tsc --noEmit` after each:\n1. First batch: family directories (imageUpscale/, videoEnhance/, zImageTurboI2I/) \u2014 simplest, no shared exports.\n2. Second batch: imageGeneration/ directory (after confirming types fully relocated).\n3. Third batch: joinClips/, individualTravelSegment/ directories.\n4. Fourth batch: travel creation files (createTravelBetweenImagesTask.ts, payloadBuilder.ts) \u2014 highest risk due to adjacent read-side files.\n5. Fifth batch: imageEditing files, crossfade, creation-only utilities.\n\n### createInpaintingTaskWorkflow.ts Double-Edit Risk\nThis file is a caller for BOTH magicEdit (T14) and maskedEdit (T15). If these tasks are done by different executors or in parallel, coordinate edits to avoid conflicts. Recommend doing T14 and T15 sequentially, or having one executor handle both.\n\n### What to Snapshot Before Migration\nBefore starting any resolver, capture the exact DB params for each task type by creating one task of each type through the current client-side path. Save these as JSON snapshots. After each resolver migration, compare the new server-generated params against the snapshot. Workers are not being changed \u2014 param compatibility is the hard constraint."

Get this right in T3 or every retry creates duplicates. The fix: client continues sending its stable idempotency_key (already at createTask.ts:39). For batch resolvers that expand 1 request into N tasks, the server derives per-task keys as `hash(clientIdempotencyKey + taskIndex)`. This is deterministic \u2014 retries produce the same N keys. Do NOT generate fresh UUIDs server-side.\n\n### Phasing Strategy\nThe plan's 7-phase structure exists for a reason \u2014 respect it:\n- **Foundation (T1-T6)** must land and be tested before any resolver. The dispatch + batch insert + response parsing form the platform.\n- **Type relocation (T7-T9)** is independent of foundation and can be parallelized with T1-T6. Do it early \u2014 it's low-risk and prevents compilation breakage when families are deleted later.\n- **Simple resolvers (T10-T12)** validate the architecture cheaply. If upscale or videoEnhance break, fix the framework before attempting complex resolvers.\n- **Cleanup (T22-T24)** is ONLY safe after ALL callers are migrated. The raw path stays alive until every family is done.\n\n### Parallelization Opportunities\n- T7, T8, T9 are fully independent of each other and of T1-T6.\n- T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T19, T20, T21 all depend only on T5 and can be parallelized.\n- T16 depends on T5 + T7; T17 depends on T5 + T9; T18 depends on T5 + T8.\n\n### Deno Compatibility Pitfalls\nThe edge function runs in Deno, not Node. When porting:\n- No `crypto.randomUUID()` without importing from std \u2014 use Deno's `crypto.randomUUID()` directly.\n- No `process.env` \u2014 use `Deno.env.get()`.\n- No relative imports without extensions \u2014 all imports need `.ts` suffix.\n- No npm packages unless already in the edge function's import map.\n\n### Deletion Safety Protocol (T23)\nDelete in small batches, running `npx tsc --noEmit` after each:\n1. First batch: family directories (imageUpscale/, videoEnhance/, zImageTurboI2I/) \u2014 simplest, no shared exports.\n2. Second batch: imageGeneration/ directory (after confirming types fully relocated).\n3. Third batch: joinClips/, individualTravelSegment/ directories.\n4. Fourth batch: travel creation files (createTravelBetweenImagesTask.ts, payloadBuilder.ts) \u2014 highest risk due to adjacent read-side files.\n5. Fifth batch: imageEditing files, crossfade, creation-only utilities.\n\n### createInpaintingTaskWorkflow.ts Double-Edit Risk\nThis file is a caller for BOTH magicEdit (T14) and maskedEdit (T15). If these tasks are done by different executors or in parallel, coordinate edits to avoid conflicts. Recommend doing T14 and T15 sequentially, or having one executor handle both.\n\n### What to Snapshot Before Migration\nBefore starting any resolver, capture the exact DB params for each task type by creating one task of each type through the current client-side path.   "meta_commentary": "## Execution Guidance\n\n### The One Thing That Can Silently Break Everything\nThe idempotency design (watch item #1) is the only open significant flag. Get this right in T3 or every retry creates duplicates. The fix: client continues sending its stable idempotency_key (already at createTask.ts:39). For batch resolvers that expand 1 request into N tasks, the server derives per-task keys as `hash(clientIdempotencyKey + taskIndex)`. This is deterministic \u2014 retries produce the same N keys. Do NOT generate fresh UUIDs server-side.\n\n### Phasing Strategy\nThe plan's 7-phase structure exists for a reason \u2014 respect it:\n- **Foundation (T1-T6)** must land and be tested before any resolver. The dispatch + batch insert + response parsing form the platform.\n- **Type relocation (T7-T9)** is independent of foundation and can be parallelized with T1-T6. Do it early \u2014 it's low-risk and prevents compilation breakage when families are deleted later.\n- **Simple resolvers (T10-T12)** validate the architecture cheaply. If upscale or videoEnhance break, fix the framework before attempting complex resolvers.\n- **Cleanup (T22-T24)** is ONLY safe after ALL callers are migrated. The raw path stays alive until every family is done.\n\n### Parallelization Opportunities\n- T7, T8, T9 are fully independent of each other and of T1-T6.\n- T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T19, T20, T21 all depend only on T5 and can be parallelized.\n- T16 depends on T5 + T7; T17 depends on T5 + T9; T18 depends on T5 + T8.\n\n### Deno Compatibility Pitfalls\nThe edge function runs in Deno, not Node. When porting:\n- No `crypto.randomUUID()` without importing from std \u2014 use Deno's `crypto.randomUUID()` directly.\n- No `process.env` \u2014 use `Deno.env.get()`.\n- No relative imports without extensions \u2014 all imports need `.ts` suffix.\n- No npm packages unless already in the edge function's import map.\n\n### Deletion Safety Protocol (T23)\nDelete in small batches, running `npx tsc --noEmit` after each:\n1. First batch: family directories (imageUpscale/, videoEnhance/, zImageTurboI2I/) \u2014 simplest, no shared exports.\n2. Second batch: imageGeneration/ directory (after confirming types fully relocated).\n3. Third batch: joinClips/, individualTravelSegment/ directories.\n4. Fourth batch: travel creation files (createTravelBetweenImagesTask.ts, payloadBuilder.ts) \u2014 highest risk due to adjacent read-side files.\n5. Fifth batch: imageEditing files, crossfade, creation-only utilities.\n\n### createInpaintingTaskWorkflow.ts Double-Edit Risk\nThis file is a caller for BOTH magicEdit (T14) and maskedEdit (T15). If these tasks are done by different executors or in parallel, coordinate edits to avoid conflicts. Recommend doing T14 and T15 sequentially, or having one executor handle both.\n\n### What to Snapshot Before Migration\nBefore starting any resolver, capture the exact DB params for each task type by creating one task of each type through the current client-side path. Save these as JSON snapshots. After each resolver migration, compare the new server-generated params against the snapshot. Workers are not being changed \u2014 param compatibility is the hard constraint."
